input.quote: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
input.rationale:
Section 20 is a one-way, unlimited Customer indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", with no Vendor indemnity at all — no IP infringement indemnity, no data-breach, law-violation or wilful-misconduct coverage, and no claim-handling procedure. This is the playbook walk-away position. Section 9.3 also cross-refers to infringement remedies "required by Section 20.5", which does not exist, confirming the omission. The redline inserts the Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Security Incident/Customer Data disclosure, injury, gross negligence/wilful misconduct), standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary IP exclusions and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at 20.5 (curing the dangling cross-reference), and narrows our indemnity to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. Indemnity obligations are already carved out of the liability cap as Excluded Claims under Section 21.3, so no super-cap fallback is needed.</parationale>

proposal.summary: Add Vendor IP/law/data/misconduct indemnity, mutual indemnity procedure, IP exclusions and infringement remedies (Section 20.5), and narrow the Customer indemnity.

We have added Vendor's defence and indemnity for IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, injury and wilful misconduct, together with a standard notice/control/cooperation procedure, customary IP exclusions and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies, and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText:
20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) a Security Incident or other unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; (d) death, bodily injury, or damage to tangible property caused by Vendor; or (e) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
20.2 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that Customer Data or other material Customer provides to Vendor infringes or misappropriates a third party's intellectual property right, or (b) Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
20.3 The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of the claim, delay excusing the indemnifying Party only to the extent it is prejudiced, shall permit the indemnifying Party to control the defence with counsel of its choice, and shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense. The indemnified Party may participate with its own counsel at its own expense. No settlement imposing a non-monetary obligation, admission of liability, or unreimbursed payment on the indemnified Party is effective without its prior written consent.
20.4 Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of a Deliverable without Vendor's approval, combination of the Services with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim would not have arisen absent the combination, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications.
20.5 If an infringement claim is made or reasonably anticipated, Vendor shall at its expense procure for Customer the right to continue using the affected item or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item. If neither remedy is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverable and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated portion and Fees paid for the affected Deliverable.
